_note: Dimensions, not personas. A project selects one value per dimension and the constraints merge: numeric floors take the MAXIMUM across selected values, forbidden lists concatenate. That is what makes 'audience floors override sector density' a computation rather than an opinion. Floors are floors: a sector may go denser than a floor allows only by declaring a deviation with a reason, the same discipline tokens use for provenance.

age.label: Age band of the primary user

children.label: Children, under about 13

forbidden.what: text-only affordances
forbidden.why: an unread label is an invisible control

forbidden.what: irreversible actions without confirmation
forbidden.why: exploration is how this audience learns, and it will find every destructive path

designImplication: icons carry meaning, labels confirm it, and neither works alone
one decision per screen; a screen with three choices gets answered by whichever is largest
children.evidence: reading grade is the hard constraint; everything else follows from it

teens.label: Teenagers, roughly 13 to 19

forbidden.what: patronising tone
forbidden.why: it is detected instantly and costs the whole product's credibility

designImplication: platform conventions can be assumed; this audience knows them better than the designer
speed of interaction outranks explicitness
teens.evidence: the only audience where under-explaining is safer than over-explaining

working-age.label: Working-age adults, roughly 20 to 64
designImplication: the default assumption, and the one worth stating rather than defaulting to silently
working-age.evidence: WCAG AA minimums with no additional band-specific floor

older-adults.label: Older adults, roughly 65 and above

forbidden.what: gesture-only actions
forbidden.why: swipe-to-reveal and long-press have no discoverable affordance and are the commonest total blocker for this band

forbidden.what: auto-dismissing messages
forbidden.why: a toast that clears in four seconds is a message that was never delivered

forbidden.what: time-limited interactions
forbidden.why: a session that expires mid-form loses work the user cannot reconstruct

forbidden.what: low-contrast placeholder text as the only label
forbidden.why: the label disappears exactly when it is needed

designImplication: every gesture has a visible control that does the same thing
errors state what to do next, not only what went wrong
motion is reduced by default rather than on request
older-adults.evidence: contrast floor is raised to WCAG AAA because age-related contrast sensitivity loss is the most reliable of the band's changes

region.label: Region and cultural context of the primary user
region._note: textExpansion is the multiplier against English at the same content. It is a layout constraint, not a translation note: a button sized to its English label breaks at 1.3.

europe-west.label: Western Europe

formats.decimal: comma in most, point in UK and Ireland
formats.name: given then family
formats.address: street then number in DE/NL, number then street in UK/FR

europe-west.formality: German, French and Dutch carry a formal register that has to be chosen deliberately; English does not
designImplication: German at 1.3 is the layout stress case for this region; size controls to it, not to English
GDPR consent is a design surface, not a footer link

europe-central.label: Central and Eastern Europe
europe-central.formality: Czech, Slovak and Polish distinguish formal and informal address; the formal is correct for financial and public services
designImplication: diacritics are load-bearing: a typeface missing them is unusable, and stripping them changes meaning
multi-currency is common and users expect currencies held apart rather than converted

north-america.label: United States and Canada
north-america.formality: informal by default across almost every sector
designImplication: accessibility is a legal exposure, not only a quality bar

east-asia.label: East Asia
east-asia.formality: Japanese and Korean encode social distance grammatically; the register is a product decision

colourDeparture.where: China, and financial markets across the region where red is up

designImplication: information density expectations are materially higher; a Western-spaced layout reads as empty and unfinished
market colour convention is inverted from Western defaults and getting it wrong reverses the meaning of every figure

southeast-asia.label: Southeast Asia

formats.decimal: comma or point, varies by country
formats.name: varies: Vietnamese is family first, Indonesian may be a single name

southeast-asia.formality: Vietnamese pronouns encode relative age and status and have no neutral default
designImplication: a single-name user is valid and a form requiring two names will exclude real people
mobile-first is not a preference here, it is the only surface for much of the audience

south-asia.label: South Asia

formats.decimal: point, with lakh and crore grouping
formats.name: highly variable; patronymics and single names both common

south-asia.formality: English is often the interface language regardless of first language
designImplication: number grouping is 2,2,3 not 3,3,3: ₹12,34,567 is correct and a thousands separator every three digits reads as wrong
multilingual switching mid-session is normal

mena.label: Middle East and North Africa
mena.formality: formal register is the default in institutional contexts
designImplication: RTL mirrors the entire layout, not the text: navigation, icons with direction, progress, and every chart axis
a layout built LTR and flipped by a stylesheet gets the icons wrong; direction has to be a design decision per element

latin-america.label: Latin America
latin-america.formality: Spanish and Portuguese both carry a formal register; usage varies sharply by country
designImplication: two family names is the norm and a single family-name field truncates real identities
Brazilian Portuguese and Spanish are not interchangeable and treating them as one locale is visible

accessibility.label: Declared accessibility needs beyond the age-band baseline

baseline.label: No declared need beyond WCAG AA

forbidden.what: colour as the only channel for meaning
forbidden.why: it fails for eight percent of men regardless of anything the project declares

designImplication: AA is the floor for every project, declared or not

low-vision.label: Low vision

forbidden.what: text baked into images
forbidden.why: it does not scale and it does not reflow

forbidden.what: fixed-height containers holding text
forbidden.why: at 200% zoom the content is clipped and nothing says so

designImplication: reflow at 200% is a layout requirement, not a browser feature

colour-blind.label: Colour vision deficiency

forbidden.what: red and green as the only distinction
forbidden.why: the commonest deficiency makes them the same colour

forbidden.what: a categorical palette above five hues
forbidden.why: adjacent categories become indistinguishable before the sixth

designImplication: every state carries shape, position or text alongside its colour

motor.label: Motor impairment

forbidden.what: drag as the only way to do something
forbidden.why: sustained precise movement is the exact capability in question

forbidden.what: hover-only disclosure
forbidden.why: it does not exist for touch or for switch access

designImplication: every drag has a non-drag equivalent, and every hover has a focus equivalent

cognitive.label: Cognitive load sensitivity

forbidden.what: time limits
forbidden.why: they convert a difficulty into a failure

forbidden.what: unannounced context change
forbidden.why: a screen that changes under the reader loses them completely

designImplication: progress is visible and reversible; every step says where it sits in the whole

screen-reader.label: Screen reader user

forbidden.what: meaning carried only by visual position
forbidden.why: the reading order is the only order that exists

forbidden.what: an icon control with no accessible name
forbidden.why: it is announced as 'button' and nothing else

designImplication: the DOM order is the design; a visual reorder that leaves it behind is a defect

literacy.label: Digital literacy of the primary user

expert-daily.label: Expert, in the product every working day
designImplication: density and shortcuts outrank explicitness; this audience resents guidance
recognition over recall stops applying — they have the recall

competent.label: Competent, uses comparable products regularly
designImplication: platform conventions can be assumed and departing from them costs something

occasional.label: Occasional, weeks or months between sessions
designImplication: every session is effectively a first session; nothing may depend on remembering last time
the main action is visible without scrolling on the screen that opens

low-digital-literacy.label: Low digital literacy

forbidden.what: conventions that are learned rather than seen
forbidden.why: a hamburger menu is not discoverable to someone who has not been taught it

forbidden.what: jargon from the business's own vocabulary
forbidden.why: the glossary is for the business, not for the screen

designImplication: affordances are explicit: a button looks pressable, a link looks like a link

conditions.label: Conditions the product is actually used in
conditions._note: This dimension accepts several values at once. A warehouse handheld is gloved AND noisy AND one-handed.

desk.label: At a desk, seated, two hands, a large screen
designImplication: the only condition where density is genuinely free

one-handed.label: One-handed, on the move

forbidden.what: primary actions in the top corners
forbidden.why: they are unreachable one-handed on a modern phone

designImplication: the primary action sits in the lower third

outdoors-bright.label: Outdoors, in direct sunlight

forbidden.what: subtle greys as a meaning channel
forbidden.why: they are invisible at 100000 lux

designImplication: the palette is tested at maximum brightness, not at a desk

gloved.label: Wearing gloves

forbidden.what: precise gestures
forbidden.why: pinch and multi-touch do not survive a glove

designImplication: nothing smaller than a fingertip through fabric

noisy.label: In a noisy environment

forbidden.what: sound as the only confirmation
forbidden.why: it is not heard

designImplication: every audible signal has a visible twin

shared-device.label: A device several people use

forbidden.what: personal data visible on an idle screen
forbidden.why: the next person sees it

designImplication: session end is a designed screen, not a timeout nobody sees
who is signed in is visible at all times

safety-critical.label: Where a mistake causes physical harm

forbidden.what: decorative use of red, amber or green
forbidden.why: those hues are inherited from site signage and spending them on decoration removes a safety channel

designImplication: the dangerous action is never adjacent to the common one
